title: DC-area forecast: Staying steamy through Friday with some showers and storms
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Just the chance of an isolated shower or storm across the DC area into early evening, then storms become more likely after 9 or 10 p.m. Partly cloudy and muggy with temperatures falling through the 80s.

What’s next? Still hot and humid Friday, with more showers and storms possible. Trending cooler and less humid for the holiday weekend.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Still only a chance for an isolated shower or storm to start the evening, then scattered showers and storms become more likely after 9 or 10 p.m. and into the overnight. Spots that see a heavier storm could pick up a quick half inch of rain or more. Under mostly cloudy skies, lows only dip to the 70s. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Friday): The front makes its way back south and lingers nearby. That may help spawn a brief morning shower or two, followed by a chance for scattered afternoon thunderstorms. Highs mainly reach the upper 80s to low 90s, and humidity remains high with dew points still near 70. Confidence: Low-Medium

Tomorrow night: Scattered showers and a thunderstorm remain a risk into the evening. Clearing the humidity out of here could still be slow, so it may stay muggy much of the night. By dawn, drier air should be more noticeable. Lows in the upper 60s to mid-70s. Confidence: Low-Medium

A look ahead

Partly sunny Saturday with decreasing humidity, but a few showers are still possible, especially west and south of DC. Highs reach the low to mid-80s. Confidence: Medium

Looking really nice Sunday into Labor Day Monday. Both days feature highs ranging from the upper 70s to low 80s most spots. Mainly sunny on Sunday, with a few more clouds for Monday. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for September 3

A powerful 1821 hurricane brought widespread coastal devastation, while in 1909 an early-season chill set record lows during a prolonged stretch of cool weather.

Today’s daily digit — 3/10: A three for Sept. 3, but mostly because of the high heat and humidity. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
